items.body:
Optimise the sparq marketing/docs SITE (site/, Next.js static export -> GitHub Pages) and the WORKBENCH (gui/, Tauri desktop app) for load+runtime perf WITHOUT introducing bugs/behavioural regressions. Levers: (a) CACHEABILITY — content-hashed immutable assets + long/immutable Cache-Control; split vendor/stable chunks so they cache across deploys; (b) REMOVE UNNECESSARY DOWNLOADS — dead code, unused/duplicate deps+polyfills, oversized assets, anything in first-load not needed on that route (lazy dynamic-import rarely-used features, per #1046/#1980); (c) PARALLELISE — chunk graph the browser fetches concurrently, preload/prefetch/modulepreload critical resources, kill request waterfalls. MEASUREMENT-FIRST (Lighthouse, bundle-analyzer, network waterfall, real first-load bytes before/after). HARD GUARDRAIL: ZERO regressions — green export+lint+typecheck+all site/gui tests+check-bundle first-load guard (no first-load byte regression)+visual/differential regression. If a root cause is UPSTREAM (Next.js chunking, a dep shipping unneeded bytes, Tauri/webview) FIX IT UPSTREAM per the upstream-contribution protocol. Relates to sq-vw3ax (site) + sq-ixc3 (GUI).

<!-- bd-id:sq-qgkwy -->

items.body:
#5022 publishes the mdBook guide at https://sparq.jeswr.org/guide/ by overlaying it into the pages.yml artifact. The mount works, but the guide is currently reachable only by typing the URL: the Next.js showcase (`site/`) has no nav entry, footer link, or route pointing at `/guide/`, and README.md does not link it either.

Out of scope for the #5022 PR, which is routed to the `ci` area and deliberately touches no `site/` source. Worth a small `site/` change adding the guide to the nav/footer (and possibly a README link).

One implementation note for whoever picks this up: pages.yml runs `scripts/check-site-links.sh` over `site/out` BEFORE the guide overlay, so a link to `/guide/` from the site's own HTML would be a dangling target for that lychee gate. Either exclude the path, or move the link-check after the overlay.

items.title: npm version is unpinned, so `npm install` on npm 10 silently rewrites the npm-11-authored package-lock.json

labels.name: status:untriaged
labels.description: Triage LLM unavailable — cron will re-triage

labels.name: self-improvement
labels.description: Agent-discovered out-of-scope work for the self-improvement triage lane

items.body:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent — out-of-scope finding while repairing CI for PR #6056.

**What.** The repo pins no npm version: repo-root `package.json` has neither a `packageManager` nor an `engines.npm` field, and `.github/workflows/*.yml` pin `node-version: 22` (which ships npm 10.9.x) without pinning npm itself. The committed `package-lock.json` on `main`, however, carries `libc` platform-selector arrays on the four `@next/swc-linux-*` optional binaries — a lockfile field npm only started writing at npm 11.

**Effect.** Any contributor or agent whose npm is 10.x rewrites the lockfile on a plain `npm install`, with no dependency actually changing: the `libc` arrays are stripped from `@next/swc-linux-{arm64,x64}-{gnu,musl}` and `fsevents` gains `"dev": true`. Reproduced directly — restoring `main`'s lockfile and running `npm install` (npm 10.9.2) regenerated the same 13-line diff byte for byte.

**Why it matters.** The churn is not cosmetic:
1. `package-lock.json` is a trigger path for `js`, `pages`, `site-e2e`, `site-e2e-foundation`, `site-e2e-hero` and `site-visual`. Touching it drags six unrelated heavyweight lanes (including visual-regression) into the required-gate surface of a PR that changes none of what they cover.
2. Dropping `libc` removes the glibc/musl selector npm >= 11 uses to choose the correct native Next.js SWC binary, so a musl-based install can resolve the wrong one.
3. It changes the runtime (`--omit=dev`) dependency view that `scripts/gen-js-sbom.sh` derives from the root lock via `scripts/derive-workspace-member-lock.mjs`.

This is not hypothetical — it is exactly what landed in PR #6056 commit `046fc565` ("repair failing CI legs", whose entire content was this lockfile churn) and had to be reverted.

**Suggested fix.** Add a `packageManager` field to the repo-root `package.json` pinning the npm version that authored the lock, and/or a CI tripwire that fails when `npm install` would modify `package-lock.json`.

> 🤖 Discovered by the SPARQ worker while implementing #2703. Out-of-scope for that PR; captured as follow-up.
<!-- sparq-followup:v1 -->

items.body:
Found while implementing the #3767 monitor.

#3767 attributes the `postcss` block (Dependabot alert #45) to `next` / `@tailwindcss/postcss` pins. That reading is wrong. The lock resolves a SINGLE hoisted `node_modules/postcss@8.5.15` with no nested copy under `next`, even though `next@15.5.21` requires `postcss` exactly `8.4.31` — which is only possible because the root `package.json` `overrides` already force it past that pin (`"postcss": "8.5.15"` plus `"next": {"postcss": "8.5.15"}`, added in 86dc0e94 for exactly this reason; sibling precedent b978324f).

So the effective blocker is OUR OWN override value, and the remediation is a one-line bump to the patched release — not an upstream wall.

Not done in the #3767 PR because it requires regenerating `package-lock.json` (new `resolved` URL + `integrity` hash) and re-verifying the `site` / `gui/app` Next.js builds; the implementing environment had no `npm`, and a hand-edited lock would be unverifiable.

What to do:
1. Bump root `overrides.postcss` (and the `next.postcss` nested override) to the patched version.
2. Reconcile `site/package.json`, which also declares a looser `postcss` override (`>=8.5.10`).
3. `npm install` to regenerate the root lock; verify with `npm ci` + `npm ls postcss` + the site/gui builds.
4. Update `supply-chain/npm-advisories.md` — the GATING `scripts/check-npm-advisory-record.py` will RED on the version + override change, by design. Close alert #45 / update #3767.

> 🤖 Discovered by the SPARQ worker while implementing #3767. Out-of-scope for that PR; captured as follow-up.
